toegepas.blok: Wat beeste vir die boere gegee het
toegepas.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the adjunct naturally stands before the past participle at the end of the clause; 'geslag vir hulle vleis' follows English order.
toegepas.fout: The purpose phrase trails after the participle in English order.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Placing 'vir hulle vleis' before 'geslag' is the natural written Afrikaans order, and the meaning and the word 'geslag' stay intact.

laat_vaar.blok: Wat beeste vir die boere gegee het
laat_vaar.voor: beeste aangehou wat hulle op baie maniere gehelp het
laat_vaar.na: beeste aangehou, en die beeste het hulle op baie maniere gehelp
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: With 'wat hulle' a young reader can briefly take 'wat' as object (the farmers helped the cattle); naming the subject removes the ambiguity, and the AWS comma is required between the two clauses.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The heading and the paragraph make 'the cattle helped the farmers' the only sensible reading, and the proposal adds a clumsy repeat of 'beeste' in a paragraph already full of it.

laat_vaar.voor: Ons sê so 'n gesin het hoë status gehad
laat_vaar.na: Ons sê dat so 'n gesin hoë status gehad het
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Written study text reads better with the full 'dat' clause and verb-final order than with the spoken form without 'dat'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Leaving out 'dat' after 'sê' is normal, natural Afrikaans, so this is a sideways change rather than a fix.

na_skrywer.na: hoeveel respek ander mense vir hom het
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'hoeveel ander mense' reads as a count of people, while the definition means the degree of respect; the new wording keeps that meaning unambiguous.
na_skrywer.fout: 'hoeveel ander mense hom respekteer' most readily reads as a count of people rather than how much respect he gets.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The ambiguity is real, but this is a glossary definition, so the rewording belongs to the writer, not a language agent.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: Protected in the sense 'man or woman' (not 'gender'), but in this lesson it appears only as the verb 'slaughtered' ('beeste ... geslag'); no change to it is proposed, and the word stays intact in the word-order change, but the entry does not really apply to this lesson.
